DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www_dilg_gov_ph DILG OPINION No. 53 s. 2023 AUG. 10, 2023 ATTY. JOE PATRICK LEONOR patrickleonor@gmail.com Dear Atty. Leonor: This has reference to your electronic mail dated June 3, 2023 seeking guidance and approval regarding the necessary requirements on your intent to practice the legal profession. Per your representations, it appears that: • You are the incumbent College President of a local college in Nueva Ecija created by the Sangguniang Panlungsod and regulated by the Commission on Higher Education (CHED); That you have already obtained a limited private practice from the Mayor but would like to be enlightened on whether an authority from the head of this agency or CHED would be necessary. At the outset, may we cite Sec. 7 (b)(2) of RA 67131 which provides that public officials and employees may practice their profession, provided that such practice will not conflict with their official functions. The pertinent provision of the said law provides: "Section 7. Prohibited Acts and Transactions. - In addition to acts and omissions of public officials and employees now prescribed in the Constitution and existing laws, the following shall constitute prohibited acts and transactions of any public official and employee and are hereby declared to be unlawful: (b) Outside employment and other activities related thereto. - Public officials and employees during their incumbency shall not: (2) Engage in the private practice of their profession unless authorized by the Constitution or law, provided, that such practice will not conflict or tend to conflict functions: with their official or (Emphasis Supplied) 1 Entitled "Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees". Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

In addition, Section 18, Rule XIII of the Revised Omnibus Rules on Appointments and Other Personnel Actions states that: "Sec. 18. Unless otherwise provided by law, no officer or employee shall engage directly or indirectly in any private business or profession without a written permission from the head of aqency. Provided that this prohibition will be absolute in the case of those officers and employees whose duties and responsibilities require that their entire time be at the disposal of the government: Provided further, that if an employee is granted permission to engage in outside activities, the time devoted outside of office hours should be fixed by the head of the agency so that it will not impair in any way the efficiency of the officer or employee nor pose a conflict or tend to conflict with the official functions." (Emphasis Supplied) Relative thereto, the Office of the President through Memorandum Circular No. 172 dated 4 September 1986 provides that the authority to grant permission to any official or employee shall be granted by the head of the ministry or agency in accordance with Sec. 12, Rule XV1113 of the Revised Civil Service Rules. In addition, the Supreme Court had on an occasion discussed the same subject matter in the case of Monares vs Mufioz4 which clarified the authority to be secured prior to engaging in private practice. Hence, applying the foregoing, we opine that in addition to the permission granted by the City Mayor, a written permission from the head of agency must still be secured. Verily, a lawyer in the government service who is not prohibited to practice law must secure prior authority from the head of his Department, which in this particular case is from the Secretary of this Department. In this regard, you are hereby advised to submit your written request and pertinent supporting documents to the DILG Secretary for this purpose. In the exercise of due diligence and to remind the members of the bar to practice the profession within the limits and bounds of the law, we quote the Supreme Court in the case of Abella vs. Atty. Cruzabra5, to wit: "Subject to any additional conditions which the head of the office deems necessary in each particular case in the interest of the service, as expressed in the various 2 The authority to grant permission to any official or employee shall be granted by the head of the ministry or agency in accordance with Section 12, Rule XVIII of the Revised Civil Service Rules, which provides: "Sec. 12. No officer or employee shall engage directly in any private business, vocation, or profession or be connected with any commercial, credit, agricultural, or industrial undertaking without a written permission from the head of Department: Provided, That this prohibition will be absolute in the case of those officers and employees whose duties and responsibilities require that their entire time be at the disposal of the Government: Provided, further, That if an employee is granted permission to engage in outside activities. the time so devoted outside of office hours should be fixed by the chief of the agency to the end that it will not impair in any way the efficiency of the officer or employee: And provided, finally, That no permission is necessary in the case of investments, made by an officer or employee, which do not involve any real or apparent conflict between his private interests and public duties, or in any way influence him in the discharge of his duties, and he shall not take part in the management of the enterprise or become an officer or member of the board of directors", 3 Sec. 12. No officer or employee shall engage directly in any private business, vocation, or profession or be connected with any commercial, credit, agricultural, or industrial undertaking without a written permission from the head of Department: Provided, That this prohibition will be absolute in the case of those officers and employees whose duties and responsibilities require that their entire time be at the disposal of the Government: Provided, further, That if an employee is granted permission to engage in outside activities, the time so devoted outside of office hours should be fixed by the chief Of the agency to the end that it will not impair in any way the efficiency of the officer or employee x x x. 4 AC No. 5582. January 24, 2017. 5 A.c. No. 5688. June 04, 2009 Page 2 of 3 CamScanner

issuances of the Civil Service Commission. It is clear that when respondent filed her petition for commission as a notary public, she did not obtain a written permission from the Secretary of the DOJ. Respondent's superior, the Register of Deeds, cannot issue any authorization because he is not the head of the Department. And even assuming that the Register of Deeds authorized her, respondent failed to present any proof of that written permission. Respondent cannot feign ignorance or good faith because respondent filed her petition for commission as a notary public after Memorandum Circular No. 17 was issued in 1986." (Emphasis Supplied) The foregoing is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinions of more competent authorities and the courts. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: VI OR R. LLAMAS ATTY. cretary for External, Legal and Legislatiye Affair JRULLLS-LRALLD/sbVclp ous copy furnished: ATTY. ANTHONY C.
